title: The integral compact-support direct image of a constructible complex is constructible
statement: Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(j,\bar f)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and let $Rf_{!,n}=R\bar f_{*,n}j_!:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ be the compact-support candidate attached to $c$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an object of the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. The objects $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}K_n$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, with $\operatorname{Res}_n$ the restriction of scalars of the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] applied termwise [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], form an inverse system whose transition map $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ applied to the composite of $Rf_{!,n+1}$ of the reduction map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}K_n$ with the isomorphism $Rf_{!,n+1}\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}\cong\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}Rf_{!,n}$ of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Then every derived limit $M=R\varprojlim_nM_n$ of this system in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$: it is derived complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the reduction $M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], with cohomological supports in one interval independent of $n$.
